title: Adaptive Risk Evaluation in FinTech Systems via Reinforcement-Based Continuous Policy Optimization
tldr: Adaptive reinforcement learning framework ARL-CPO achieves 97.4% prediction accuracy and 98.8% trend adaptation rate for real-time FinTech risk evaluation using continuous policy optimization.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional risk assessment methods are batch-trained and cannot adapt continuously to concept drift in financial environments. Existing supervised approaches lack continuous policy refinement in response to streaming drift, leaving a gap for deployable, observable, and production-safe adaptive risk pipelines. The research gap is not only algorithmic but also a missing software capability.
approach: Formulates risk evaluation as a continuous-action Markov Decision Process with continuous state and action spaces.
Proposes ARL-CPO with dual-module actor-critic design: policy learning module and value estimation module.
Uses streaming transactional and behavioral data with outcome-driven reward feedback for continuous policy updates.
Separates online learning from inference serving to enable modular approach for integrating ARL into production risk pipelines.
Evaluates on synthetic dataset of 8.5 million credit records generated in a custom FinTech environment simulator.
Compares against Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Transformer baselines across prediction accuracy, trend adaptation, and long-term performance.
findings: num: 97.4% classification accuracy, outperforming baselines by over 18%.
num: 98.8% trend adaptation rate, indicating high responsiveness to distributional shifts.
num: 96.1% cumulative long-term performance index, demonstrating sustained performance optimization.
ARL-CPO shows continuous improvement over training epochs while baselines plateau.
Continuous action formulation allows fine-grained, context-sensitive risk quantification.
Dual-module architecture enables stable convergence under distributional shift without catastrophic forgetting.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes a reinforcement learning framework for adaptive risk evaluation that addresses the limitation of batch-trained models in non-stationary financial environments. It proposes a continuous-action MDP formulation with dual-module actor-critic design that enables online policy updates without service interruption. The work provides both algorithmic innovation and software engineering architecture for deploying adaptive risk scoring in production FinTech systems. The empirical evaluation demonstrates superior performance over traditional methods in prediction accuracy, trend adaptation, and long-term cumulative performance.
directly_justifies: Reinforcement learning can solve sequential decision making and long-horizon goals not addressed by prediction-only models.
Continuous policy optimization removes batch-retraining latency enabling real-time adaptation.
Dual-module separation allows stable convergence under distributional shift.
Reward-based sequential optimization focuses on cumulative risk reduction rather than myopic predictions.
ARL-CPO achieves 97.4% classification accuracy outperforming baselines by over 18%.
limits: Study constrained by use of synthetic dataset and simulated environment.
Operational constraints, feedback delays, and compliance requirements in real deployments may vary significantly.
More testing needed on public or production datasets for real-world generalization.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all topic domains identified relevant coverage in domains 4 (existing systems), 5 (behavioral profiles), 6 (predictive modeling), 12 (evaluation frameworks), and 14 (synthetic data and model serving). Domain 4.A and 4.B are relevant as the paper reviews existing risk assessment methods and identifies gaps. Domain 5.A is relevant through use of behavioral risk signals. Domain 6.A is core as the paper proposes predictive modeling for credit risk. Domains 12.A and 12.B are highly relevant due to comprehensive evaluation framework. Domain 14.A is relevant due to synthetic data generation, and 14.B due to deployment architecture. Domains 1-3 (Filipino demographics, cultural practices, expense categorization) were considered and rejected as not relevant. Domains 7-11 (budgeting, anomaly detection, mobile design, privacy, engagement) were considered and rejected as not directly addressed. Domain 13 (savings/debt management) was considered but rejected as the paper focuses on risk evaluation rather than personal finance management.
